record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.original_question: Let E be a non-normable separable Frechet space, and let L(E) denote its continuous linear operators. Does there exist an operator T in L(E) such that, for every nonzero complex scalar lambda, the scalar multiple lambda T is hypercyclic? Here an operator S is hypercyclic if some vector x has dense orbit {S^n x : n in N}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a separable, non-normable Fréchet space, and let $L(E)$ denote the algebra of continuous linear operators on $E$. An operator $S \in L(E)$ is called hypercyclic if there exists a vector $x \in E$ whose orbit $\{S^n x : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ is dense in $E$.

Does there exist an operator $T \in L(E)$ such that, for every nonzero complex scalar $\lambda \in \mathbb{C} \setminus \{0\}$, the operator $\lambda T$ is hypercyclic?
artifact.status_search_result: In the Banach space setting, a theorem of León-Saavedra and Müller implies that every nonzero scalar multiple of a hypercyclic operator is hypercyclic, so such operators exist on any separable infinite-dimensional Banach space. For non-normable separable Fréchet spaces the corresponding rotation/scalar invariance is more delicate, and no published resolution of the existence question in this exact form was located in the search; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hypercyclic sequences of operators - León-Saavedra, Müller
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys conditions implying hypercyclicity of sequences (T_n), with the particular case (λ_n T).
status_evidence.claim: Foundational Banach-space result that every nonzero scalar multiple of a hypercyclic operator is hypercyclic.

status_evidence.title: Hypercyclic Operators on Non-normable Fréchet Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Every infinite-dimensional separable non-normable Fréchet space admits a continuous hypercyclic operator.
status_evidence.claim: Hypercyclic operators exist on non-normable separable Fréchet spaces, but the scalar-multiple invariance question is treated separately and not resolved here.
